source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "ដំណាំល្ហុង" (Papaya Cultivation), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
Once the prepared planting holes have rested for a few days, the papaya seedling is transplanted into the hole and the soil firmed gently around its base to protect the young roots.

Around the time of transplanting, the source describes spraying a pest-control mixture — about 30 cc mixed into 16 liters of water — over the young seedlings to protect them from insects that attack the stems and leaves shortly after planting.
caveat: The exact product name for the 30cc/16L spray was not clearly legible in the source (it is referred to only generically as a pest-control mixture); the specific active ingredient and target pest are not confirmed and should not be assumed.
